declaration.negotiation_history_statement: Whitcombe Reyes LLP proposed a $32 million class fund with automatic payments to identified class members, together with $2 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. The proposal contained no clear-sailing provision and directed any fees not awarded by the court to the class rather than Brightline. Defense counsel accepted that proposal in the first round. There were no counteroffers or further negotiations. The class fund and fee terms were proposed at the same time, not negotiated sequentially. The $32 million fund represents half of the $64 million in disputed charges and provides direct recovery without requiring claims. In assessing the settlement, counsel considered the risks of class certification and trial, the likely delay of two to three years before trial, and counsel’s estimate of a 55% chance of prevailing at trial with a likely $50 million award if successful. The firm receives a fixed $3.5 million under a separate foundation-funded engagement regardless of the outcome; any settlement fee awarded is paid to the foundation, not the firm. The proposed settlement remains subject to the court’s approval.
